questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to find and sell valuable old Pokémon cards
The history of the World Wide Web and its inventor
Why famous paintings are so valuable at auctions
What NFTs are and why people disagree about them
questions.why: They explain non-fungible tokens and discuss the strong opinions on both sides of the NFT debate.

questions.q: What did Sam collect in the past?
options: Stamps
Football stickers
Pokémon cards
Comics
questions.why: Sam says he used to have a big collection of Pokémon cards.

questions.q: Why does Neil talk about swapping a £10 note for two £5 notes?
options: To explain what 'fungible' means
To show how cheap NFTs are
To explain how to pay for NFTs
To compare pounds with dollars
questions.why: Neil uses money as an example of something fungible, which can be interchanged with the same value.

questions.q: According to Neil, why do collectors want NFTs?
options: Because they can hang them on the wall
Because they want something nobody else has
Because they are always cheap
Because they can swap them for money
questions.why: He says collectors want something no-one else has, even though they own nothing physical.

questions.q: What example does Neil give of the rising value of NFTs?
options: A copy of the Mona Lisa sold for millions
A Pokémon card sold for £2,500
A signed football shirt sold online
A digital sticker of Kylian Mbappé sold for £25,000
questions.why: Neil says a digital sticker of Kylian Mbappé recently sold for £25,000.

questions.q: What does Sam say about Sir Tim Berners-Lee and the World Wide Web?
options: He became a billionaire by selling advertising on it
He never made money from it and wanted it free for all
He sold it to a large American technology company
He charged every user a small fee to go online
questions.why: Sam says he never made money from the web, insisting it should be free for everyone.

questions.q: What is Shona Ghosh's view of NFTs?
options: They are the safest way for ordinary people to invest
They should be banned immediately by all governments
They are a new area with no rules and very high prices
They are only popular with young people who play games
questions.why: She calls NFTs 'a wild west' where digital collectables go for lots of money.

questions.q: According to Rory Cellan-Jones, why do some people criticise NFTs?
options: They may be a dishonest scheme and harm the environment
They are too difficult and expensive for most people to buy
They are only bought and sold by celebrities and the rich
They lose most of their value within a few weeks of sale
questions.why: He says to others they're a dubious pyramid scheme with a damaging impact on the environment.
